rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 Materials and methods and Tables 1-2 report the authors' own two-year field experiment (2003, 2006) at the Harran University research farm comparing water pillow irrigation at three levels with furrow irrigation for soybean, with measured yield, applied water, ET, gravimetric soil water and soil temperature at 20 cm.
rows.notes: The study tests a water pillow (WP) system, a gravity-fed perforated black polyethylene pipe laid on the soil surface, not drip irrigation under plastic mulch (DIPM). The instructions name this exact case as a technology mismatch, so Q2 is 'no'. What the study actually shows for the WP system: pre-irrigation soil water content was higher under WP1.0 and WP0.75 than under furrow irrigation (Section 3.1), and soil temperature at 20 cm was 1.4-2.0 degrees C higher under WP than FI (Section 3.3, Fig. 6). Nothing on nutrient availability is measured. The soil temperature/moisture results are from a single clay-loam site and one crop, with no dispersion measures reported.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2 and Tables 1-2 report the authors' own two-year field trial of water pillow versus furrow irrigation on soybean with measured yield, water use and soil temperature.
rows.notes: Two reasons for Q2 'no'. First, the technology is the water pillow pipe, not drip irrigation under plastic mulch (technology mismatch per instructions). Second, the study does not measure weed density, weed growth or herbicide use at all; the statements in Section 3.1 and the Conclusions that WP reduces weed density, restricts weed growth and decreases herbicide use are attributed to B<U+00FC>k<U+00FC>n et al. (2005) or asserted without data from this trial. The study's own results concern yield, yield components, ET, WUE/IWUE, soil water and soil temperature only.

notes: Full text appears complete (Agricultural Water Management 96 (2009) 87-92). The study is a single-site, single-crop (soybean cv. Merill A-3935), two-season plot experiment on clay loam in semi-arid Sanliurfa, Turkey, comparing a patented water pillow irrigation system with furrow irrigation. Neither claim row concerns the technology actually tested, so both rows are rated as technology mismatches regardless of the quality of the WP results.
